entry.title: how to Handle a Assertion_failed Dump in SAP ABAP ?
entry.content:
Hi Experts,

We have a custom ABAP report running in background (SM37) that loops through a set of sales orders and updates them using SD_SALESDOCUMENT_CHANGE alongside custom BAPI extensions (BAPE_VBAP) and pricing conditions.

While standard catchable exceptions (CX_ROOT) are safely handled by our TRY...CATCH blocks, we occasionally encounter hard kernel short dumps such as ASSERTION_FAILED inside standard SAP classes (e.g., CL_SD_SLS_TRANS_MGR=>IF_SD_SLS_TRANS_MGR_INT~SET_TRANSACTION_STATE). Because these assertions trigger an immediate kernel abort, they bypass our TRY...CATCH blocks and crash the entire background job.

My Questions:

Since standard class assertions without checkpoint groups cannot be caught via TRY...CATCH or CX_SY_ASSERT, what is the recommended ABAP design pattern to isolate such failures?

entry.title: Building an ATC-Based Transport Release Assistant with AI Code Suggestions in SAP GUI (ECC)?
entry.content:
Hi SAP ABAP Community,

I'm currently developing a custom ABAP tool and would appreciate feedback from experienced SAP developers on whether this solution is useful, whether similar functionality already exists in SAP ECC, and whether my proposed UI architecture is technically feasible.

Background

I've heard that in SAP S/4HANA Cloud, Public Edition, certain development and transport processes can enforce ATC checks before changes are released or deployed.

This made me wonder:

Is there any standard functionality in SAP ECC / SAP GUI that prevents a transport request from being released until specific ATC or Code Inspector findings are resolved?

If such functionality already exists, I'd like to understand it before continuing with a custom solution.

What I've developed so far

I'm currently testing this on an SAP_BASIS 740 system using SAP GUI.

My prototype can:

Read an ABAP program and check whether it has opted in for review.

Execute Code Inspector checks programmatically using ABAP classes.

Extract findings, including severity, check description, source line, and surrounding source-code context.

Store the execution results in custom database tables (ZOKG_LOG_HDR and ZOKG_LOG_ITEM).

Identify a program with findings and automatically open it in the standard SE38 ABAP Editor in Change mode.

Display a separate AI Code Review screen using CL_GUI_CUSTOM_CONTAINER and CL_GUI_TEXTEDIT, with a Copy Code button.

Currently, the AI code is sample output. Integration with an LLM to generate actual corrections is planned.

The longer-term goal is to integrate this with the CTS transport-release process using IF_EX_CTS_REQUEST_CHECK~CHECK_BEFORE_RELEASE, so that relevant findings can be reviewed before releasing a transport request.

Current limitation: Two SAP GUI sessions

At present, my tool opens two separate SAP GUI sessions:

Session 1: The actual SE38 ABAP Editor, with the target program opened in Change mode.

Session 2: My custom AI review screen displaying suggested code.

This works, but I would prefer to provide the entire review experience within the SE38 window.

What I want to achieve

When my tool opens a program in SE38, I would like a dialog box to open automatically within that same SAP GUI session.

The dialog would contain a tabstrip with two tabs:

Tab 1 — AI Suggested Code

Display the AI-generated corrected ABAP code in a read-only editor, with an option to copy the suggested code. The developer can review the suggestion and manually apply the changes in SE38.

Tab 2 — ATC / Code Inspector Findings

Display the findings for the current program, including severity, description, line number, and relevant source-code context.

I would also like to add a button to the SE38 toolbar, such as AI / ATC Review.

The expected behavior would be:

The review dialog opens automatically when the program is opened through my tool.

The developer can close the dialog and continue working in SE38.

The SE38 editor remains open.

The developer can click the AI / ATC Review button at any time to reopen the dialog.

My technical questions

Existing functionality: Does SAP ECC already provide a standard ATC or Code Inspector-based transport-release gate? Are there established alternatives such as CTS checks or transport quality gates?

SE38 enhancement: Is there any supported BAdI, customer exit, enhancement point, or API that allows a custom dialog and toolbar button to be integrated into the standard SE38 ABAP Editor?

GUI session handling: Since RS_TOOL_ACCESS with IN_NEW_WINDOW = 'X' opens the editor in another SAP GUI session, is there a supported way to initialize and reopen a custom dialog from within that editor session?

Architecture: Would you recommend extending the standard SE38 interface, developing a custom editor/review transaction, or keeping the current two-session approach?

Project value: Do you think a tool combining pre-release ATC checks, source-code context, AI suggestions, and developer-controlled corrections would be useful in an ECC development environment?

I'm trying to keep the implementation maintainable and avoid modifications to SAP standard objects.

I'd appreciate any suggestions, relevant SAP documentation, existing tools, or alternative approaches.

Thanks in advance!

entry.title: How to Expose Parameterized CDS Views as an OData Service in SAP S/4HANA Public Cloud RAP for Fiori
entry.content:
Hello Experts,

We are developing a custom Raw Material Report in SAP S/4HANA Public Cloud using the RAP and SAP Fiori Elements App.

As per the business requirements, the report contains 10 fields, including Raw Material and various quantity fields such as Opening Quantity, Issued Quantity, and Purchase Order Quantity. The quantity fields must be calculated based on the user selected date range, with the relevant quantities aggregated for each material within the specified period.

To achieve this requirement, I have implemented parameterized CDS views to fetch and aggregate the data based on the selected date range. However, while attempting to expose these CDS views through the Service Definition and Service Binding, I encountered an issue because the parameterized CDS views are not directly supported for OData service exposure in the current approach.

As a result, I am unable to create OData service, which is blocking the deployment of the Fiori Elements application.

Could you please suggest an alternative solution to handle the date  dependent calculations and expose the CDS view data through an OData service in SAP S/4HANA Public Cloud?

Please find attached a screenshot of the parameterized CDS view for your reference.

Thank you

entry.title: SAP TM 9.6 SP11 – Standard API/BAPI/FM to Create Rate Values and New Validity Periods Programmatical
entry.content:
Hello SAP Community,

I am working on a custom ABAP report in SAP Transportation Management (SAP TM 9.6 SP11) to automate the upload of linehaul rates from an Excel file provided by carriers.

The requirement is to update existing rate tables by creating new validity periods and adding the corresponding rate values.

The expected functionality includes:

  1. Identifying the existing active validity period for a rate table.

  2. Updating the existing Valid To date to one day before the new Valid From date.

  3. Creating a new validity period with the required Valid From and Valid To dates.

  4. Adding the required calculation rule and rate values.

  5. Saving and releasing the rate table.

  6. Implementing error handling and delta-run functionality to reprocess failed records.

I have investigated the standard report /SCMTMS/TCC_RATES_EXCEL_NEW and the function module /SCMTMS/WRITE_RATE_RFC, but I have not yet identified a suitable, supported API for implementing the complete requirement directly from my custom report.

I would appreciate guidance on the following questions:

  • Is there a standard BAPI, function module, or class available in SAP TM 9.6 SP11 to create or update rate values and validity periods programmatically?

  • Can the /scmtms/tc_rates BOPF business object be used for this requirement? If so, which nodes, actions, or APIs should be investigated?

  • Is there a supported way to reuse the standard Excel upload processing without manually reproducing its logic?

  • Can /SCMTMS/RATE_MASS_UPDATE handle this scenario, or is it intended for a different use case?

  • Are there any relevant SAP Notes, documentation, or working implementation examples available?

My preference is to use standard SAP functionality wherever possible rather than directly updating database tables or implementing unsupported persistence logic.

Any technical guidance or examples specific to SAP TM 9.6 would be greatly appreciated.

Thank you.

entry.title: Exit to Create a Debit/Credit Memo in VA01 with reference to a BIlling Document
entry.content:
Hello Experts,

When creating a debit/credit memo in transaction VA01 with reference to a billing document, the system automatically copies the items, materials, and properties, and correctly updates the document flow (showing the preceding billing document, goods receipt, etc.) when viewed in VA03.

I am currently facing a requirement where I need to create a debit/credit memo via VA01 **without** using the standard reference to a billing document (i.e., created in "normal" mode), but I still need the document flow to link back to that specific billing document.

To achieve this, I attempted to use the user exit `USEREXIT_SAVE_DOCUMENT_PREPARE` by populating the following internal structures:

- **XVBFA (Document Flow):**
- VBELV: Billing document number (preceding document)
- POSNV: Billing document item
- VBELN: Left empty (assigned by the system upon saving)
- POSNN: Debit/credit memo item
- VBTYP_V: 'M' (Invoice)
- VBTYP_N: 'H' (Returns / Credit Memo depending on config)
- RFMNG, MEINS, RFWRT, WAERS, ERDAT, ERZET
- UPDKZ: 'I' (Insert)

- **XVBAK (Header):**
- VGBEL: Reference billing document number
- VGTYP: 'M' (Invoice)

- **XVBAP (Items):**
- VGPOS: Reference billing document item
- UPDKZ: 'U' (Update)

But when I check the document flow in VA03 after saving, the reference to the billing document does not appear; I only see the debit/credit memo itself.

Has anyone faced a similar requirement? Is there an alternative user exit, BAdI, or specific field combination required to force the document flow and reference fields to persist when creating a document without direct reference?
